access_continuity_justification: docs/continuity.md is exactly this document: assets and their recovery paths, a break-glass procedure for the tag-minting App, a succession plan, and an explicit list of deliberate single points of failure. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/continuity.md
accessibility_best_practices_justificati: The project produces no user interface — the deliverable is a container image with no web pages, GUI or interactive client.
assurance_case_justification: https://github.com/CarlAllenn/monumental-archive-db/blob/main/docs/assurance-case.md — threat model in order of exposure, the four supply-chain substitution points, explicit out-of-scope boundaries, the five trust boundaries, secure design principles tied to mechanisms, a table of common implementation weaknesses with countermeasures and evidence, and a closing section naming the residual risks honestly rather than claiming there are none.
automated_integration_testing_justificat: Integration testing by construction — the suite boots the assembled image and queries a live PostgreSQL server rather than testing anything in isolation. It runs on every push and pull request through the CI workflow, and in the publish pipeline it runs per-architecture on native amd64 and arm64 runners and then again on the published bytes pulled back from the registry by digest. Every run reports success or failure as a required status check: https://github.com/CarlAllenn/monumental-archive-db/actions
build_common_tools_justification: Docker/BuildKit driven by Task, with the whole toolchain version-pinned by mise in strict/locked mode.
build_floss_tools_justification: The image can be built entirely with FLOSS tools.
build_justification: The software is a container image built from the Dockerfile with BuildKit; the continuous publish builds it on native runners, and README 'Development' gives the one-line local build. https://github.com/monumental-archive/monumental-archive-db/blob/main/README.md#development
build_non_recursive_justification: There is no recursive build system — a single Dockerfile driven by one Task target.
build_preserve_debug_justification: Nothing is compiled here, so there is no debugging-information setting to preserve.
build_repeatable_justification: Every input is pinned, so the same commit rebuilds to the same content: both FROM lines are pinned by digest and BuildKit fails closed on any mismatch rather than warning, apt package versions are exact pins under the ARG *_VERSION convention so a missing version fails the install rather than silently resolving newer, the toolchain is pinned by mise.lock in strict/locked mode, and the publish path carries no build cache of any kind, so there is no second unreviewed source of layer content. Nothing is compiled, so there is no compiler nondeterminism to control for. Note the deliberate exception: the weekly cache-free rebuild re-resolves the transitive OS layer from trixie-security on purpose — that is the remediation mechanism (https://github.com/CarlAllenn/monumental-archive-db/blob/main/docs/decisions/0001-own-the-installation.md), and it changes inputs rather than making identical inputs produce different output.
build_reproducible_justification: Honest miss, and deliberately distinguished from build_repeatable. Every input is pinned — both FROM lines by digest with BuildKit failing closed, apt versions exactly, the toolchain by mise.lock, and no cache anywhere in the publish path — but the project has never demonstrated that two independent rebuilds of the same commit produce a bit-for-bit identical image, and this criterion asks for exactly that. The known obstacles are layer timestamps (addressable with SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH and buildx rewrite-timestamp) and Debian-side nondeterminism in dpkg status ordering and ldconfig caches (harder). Worth noting that this does not conflict with the weekly cache-free rebuild: that deliberately changes inputs to refresh the OS layer, whereas reproducibility is about identical inputs yielding identical bytes.
build_standard_variables_justification: No native binaries are generated. Nothing is compiled in this repository: the image installs prebuilt PGDG packages and copies a prebuilt extension out of a digest-pinned build stage, so there are no CC, CFLAGS or LDFLAGS invocations to honour.
bus_factor_justification: The bus factor is 1 — a single maintainer. Recorded plainly in docs/slsa-reference.md as headcount-blocked, with docs/continuity.md carrying the succession and break-glass paths that exist precisely because of it. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/continuity.md
code_of_conduct_justification: The org CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md is served to this repository as a default community health file (README.md says so). https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md
code_review_standards_justification: GOVERNANCE.md section 'Code review' documents how review is conducted and what must be checked: that the change does what it says, that the claim it makes is one its checks actually enforce, that it does not weaken a documented control, and that documentation changed alongside behaviour - with the mechanical floor (formatting, linting, licence headers, commit shape, tests) left to the CI gate rather than the reviewer. What is required to be acceptable is stated too: a green gate, resolved review threads enforced by ruleset, a DCO sign-off on every commit, and a PR title and body fit to become the permanent squash commit. It also records that with one maintainer there is no second human reviewer, and names the gate as the compensating control. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#code-review
coding_standards_enforced_justification: Enforced mechanically and twice over: lefthook git hooks run the full lint suite on every commit, and required status checks on main run the same tasks in the same order. There are no bypass flags, and personal overrides are confined to a gitignored lefthook-local.yml.
coding_standards_justification: The coding standard is executable and delivered by the org belt: hadolint, shellcheck and shfmt, actionlint, zizmor, yamllint, rumdl, taplo, typos and editorconfig-checker, each passed its config at run time so no repository copy can drift; Conventional Commits are enforced at commit-msg. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#requirements-for-acceptable-contributions
contribution_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md documents the process explicitly: fork/branch, conventional imperative commit subjects under 72 columns enforced by committed, DCO sign-off, `mise run ci` green locally, pull request, squash merge. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
contribution_requirements_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md's 'Requirements for acceptable contributions' section: every change arrives by pull request, must pass `mise run ci` (the coding standard in executable form), uses Conventional Commits with imperative lowercase subjects, and is squash-merged. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
contributors_unassociated_justification: A single-maintainer project cannot have two significant contributors from different organisations. This is a head-count fact, not a hygiene gap, and it is named as a structural limit in https://github.com/CarlAllenn/monumental-archive-db/blob/main/docs/assurance-case.md
copyright_per_file_justification: The repository is REUSE 3.3 compliant: every file carries an SPDX-FileCopyrightText header, with REUSE.toml covering what cannot take a comment, and reuse lint runs as its own CI job (25/25 passing). https://github.com/CarlAllenn/monumental-archive-db/blob/main/REUSE.toml

dco_justification: Developer Certificate of Origin 1.1. Every commit must carry Signed-off-by; the commit-msg hook catches it locally and lint:dco enforces it in the gate, with no exemption list — the release commit and Renovate sign off too. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
delivery_mitm_justification: Delivered over HTTPS from GHCR; consumers pin digests and verify the org signer's build provenance with the README's gh attestation verify command. https://github.com/monumental-archive/monumental-archive-db/blob/main/README.md#verifying-a-digest
delivery_unsigned_justification: Digests, signatures and attestations are all retrieved over HTTPS from GHCR and Sigstore. Nothing is fetched over plain HTTP, and the image's own FROM lines are digest-pinned so BuildKit fails closed on any substitution.
dependency_monitoring_justification: Renovate under the org preset monitors every pin, dependency-review runs on every pull request, and every publish refuses to push while an advisory in the image's SBOM is undecided; the weekly cache-free rebuild refreshes the OS layer nobody can pin.
description_good_justification: The README opens by stating what it is: the Monumental Archive's PostgreSQL image — official postgres:18 (Debian trixie) plus exactly three audited extensions, PostGIS, pgaudit and edtf_postgres. https://github.com/CarlAllenn/monumental-archive-db#readme
documentation_achievements_justification: The README badge row identifies and links the project's achievements: CI, publish, OpenSSF Scorecard, licence, and this OpenSSF Best Practices badge. https://github.com/CarlAllenn/monumental-archive-db#readme
documentation_architecture_justification: https://github.com/CarlAllenn/monumental-archive-db/blob/main/docs/assurance-case.md#trust-boundaries — the publish boundary, the build-stage boundary, the apt boundary, the privilege boundary inside the image and the registry identity boundary. The decision register at https://github.com/CarlAllenn/monumental-archive-db/blob/main/docs/decisions/ records the load-bearing architectural choices.
documentation_basics_justification: README plus a full doc pack: CONTRIBUTING, SECURITY, GOVERNANCE, CODE_OF_CONDUCT, docs/roadmap.md, docs/assurance-case.md and a decision register at docs/decisions/. https://github.com/CarlAllenn/monumental-archive-db#readme
documentation_current_justification: Documentation is updated in the same pull request as the change it describes. Documents that name a digest or a version are explicitly tracked as things that can rot without failing anything, and are called out in CONTRIBUTING as a standing contribution opportunity; a documentation defect is treated as a bug.
documentation_interface_justification: The external interface is the published image, documented in the README: image name, tag policy, the baked CMD (shared_preload_libraries=pg_stat_statements,pgaudit and wal_level=logical), the non-root USER postgres, and the emptied /docker-entrypoint-initdb.d. Environment variables are the official postgres image's and are documented upstream.
documentation_quick_start_justification: README: for consumers, the image reference and the gh attestation verify command ('Where the image is published', 'Verifying a digest'); for developers, mise install then mise run ci, and a two-line build and smoke of the image. https://github.com/monumental-archive/monumental-archive-db/blob/main/README.md
documentation_roadmap_justification: https://github.com/CarlAllenn/monumental-archive-db/blob/main/docs/roadmap.md — what the project will and will not do over roughly the next year, with the exclusions use-case-gated rather than absolute.
documentation_security_justification: docs/assurance-case.md states the security claims and the evidence that they hold, README 'What the image asserts' lists the properties a user may rely on, and the org SECURITY.md scopes what is in and out. https://github.com/monumental-archive/monumental-archive-db/blob/main/docs/assurance-case.md
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: Nothing is compiled in this repository, so there is no build of ours in which to enable assertions.
dynamic_analysis_justification: Honest miss. Every build boots the actual artifact and exercises a live PostgreSQL server — per-architecture on native runners, and again on the bytes pulled back from the registry by digest — but that smoke test asserts fixed facts rather than varying its inputs, and there is no branch-coverage figure to qualify it under this criterion's alternative. No fuzzer is applied here. The image does ship a parser (edtf_postgres), so fuzzing EDTF strings through SQL against the booted container is a genuine option and is being tracked; note that the same parser is already fuzzed upstream in CarlAllenn/edtf with coverage-guided libFuzzer and a shared corpus, so doing it here would test this project's packaging of it rather than the parser itself.
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: No memory-unsafe code is authored here; the only executable content written in this repository is two shell scripts.
english_justification: All documentation and discussion are in English.
enhancement_responses_justification: Enhancement requests are answered on the tracker. The roadmap states scope boundaries explicitly (https://github.com/CarlAllenn/monumental-archive-db/blob/main/docs/roadmap.md, Will not do), so a refusal comes with a documented reason rather than silence.
external_dependencies_justification: Every dependency is an explicit, machine-readable pin in https://github.com/CarlAllenn/monumental-archive-db/blob/main/Dockerfile — two digest-pinned FROM lines and exact apt versions in ARG *_VERSION declarations, each with a # renovate: comment above it so the pin cannot silently lose automated coverage. Toolchain dependencies are pinned in mise.toml and mise.lock.
governance_justification: GOVERNANCE.md documents the decision model explicitly rather than aspirationally: one maintainer deciding in the open, significant decisions made in writing and in public before they are implemented (the docs-first standup, recorded as issues and pull requests), declined paths recorded with reasons so they are re-litigated against the record, and a written succession plan. It is served from the organisation's .github repository as a default community health file, so it governs every repository that does not carry its own. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md
hardened_site_justification: The project site, repository and download site are GitHub and GHCR. Checked against the live response for https://github.com/monumental-archive/monumental-archive-db on 2026-11-16: strict-transport-security max-age=31536000; includeSubdomains; preload, content-security-policy default-src 'none', x-frame-options deny, x-content-type-options nosniff.
hardening_justification: The server runs as USER postgres with no root phase and no setuid path to one, because gosu is deleted; /docker-entrypoint-initdb.d is emptied; workflows default to contents: read with per-job scopes annotated inline; runners enforce egress-policy: block; every checkout sets persist-credentials: false. https://github.com/CarlAllenn/monumental-archive-db/blob/main/docs/assurance-case.md#secure-design-principles
implement_secure_design_justification: https://github.com/CarlAllenn/monumental-archive-db/blob/main/docs/assurance-case.md#secure-design-principles — economy of mechanism (the deliverable is about 95 lines of Dockerfile and a smoke script, so most defect classes are absent because the code that would contain them was never written), fail-safe defaults (digest pins fail closed in BuildKit, exact apt pins fail rather than resolve newer, the server starts non-root and cannot be talked into root because gosu is deleted), complete mediation (one publish path, one signing identity, no manual publish route, no cache), and least privilege (contents: read by default with per-job scopes annotated inline, egress-policy: block on runners, no long-lived credential in existence).
input_validation_justification: The delivered artifact validates all client input: PostgreSQL's parser and type system reject malformed input by construction, and the one validation surface this project deliberately adds — edtf_postgres — is a strict, fail-closed EDTF validator, chosen precisely so the database and the archive's web layer cannot diverge in what they accept. Stated plainly for provenance: none of that validation code is authored in this repository, and this repository's own executable content (two shell scripts) takes no untrusted input at all.
installation_common_justification: docker pull ghcr.io/carlallenn/monumental-archive-db@<digest> — the standard installation convention for this artifact type. Uninstalling is docker rmi. The README documents the reference and the tag policy.
installation_development_quick_justifica: README 'Development': mise trust && mise install && mise run hooks:install once, then mise run ci runs the whole gate. https://github.com/monumental-archive/monumental-archive-db/blob/main/README.md#development
installation_standard_variables_justific: The image honours the official postgres image's conventions unchanged: PGDATA and the /var/lib/postgresql/data volume determine where data is written, and the consumer selects the mount. The project overrides none of them.
interact_justification: README 'Development' says contribution, security reporting, conduct and governance are the organisation's, served from monumental-archive/.github, and links them; issues and pull requests are on this repository. https://github.com/monumental-archive/monumental-archive-db/blob/main/README.md#development
interfaces_current_justification: The image tracks the current PostgreSQL major (18) on the official image, with no deprecated interfaces in use. The PostgreSQL 19 move is a tracked, deliberately gated roadmap item rather than an automatic bump: https://github.com/CarlAllenn/monumental-archive-db/blob/main/docs/roadmap.md
internationalization_justification: No user-facing strings are authored in this repository. Localisation in the delivered artifact is PostgreSQL's own, upstream and unmodified.
know_common_errors_justification: https://github.com/CarlAllenn/monumental-archive-db/blob/main/docs/assurance-case.md#common-implementation-weaknesses-countered — a table of weakness classes, the countermeasure for each, and the evidence.
know_secure_design_justification: The design argument is written down rather than asserted: https://github.com/CarlAllenn/monumental-archive-db/blob/main/docs/assurance-case.md#secure-design-principles covers economy of mechanism, fail-safe defaults, complete mediation, defence in depth and least privilege, each tied to the concrete mechanism that implements it.
license_location_justification: https://github.com/CarlAllenn/monumental-archive-db/blob/main/LICENSE at the top level. The repository is additionally REUSE 3.3 compliant (REUSE.toml, LICENSES/, SPDX headers in every file), with reuse lint enforced as its own CI job.
license_per_file_justification: Every tracked file's licence is declared by REUSE.toml, whose annotation assigns AGPL-3.0-only to every path; lint:reuse proves full REUSE 3.3 compliance in the gate on every pull request, and api.reuse.software reports the repository compliant. https://github.com/monumental-archive/monumental-archive-db/blob/main/REUSE.toml
maintained_justification: Actively maintained. Beyond ordinary commits, a scheduled cache-free rebuild republishes weekly and Renovate raises pin bumps continuously.
maintenance_or_update_justification: The supported image is the latest published digest, rebuilt on every merge and weekly (README 'Where the image is published', 'Tags'). The upgrade path is a digest bump, which Renovate raises against :latest; because consumers pin digests, an upgrade is always deliberate and reversible. https://github.com/monumental-archive/monumental-archive-db/blob/main/README.md#tags
no_leaked_credentials_justification: gitleaks runs on every commit via git hooks and over the full history in CI (task scan:secrets). Structurally, there is no long-lived publishing credential to leak: GHCR authentication uses the workflow run's own token and signing is keyless via Sigstore OIDC. Every checkout sets persist-credentials: false.
osps_ac_01_01_justification: GitHub has required two-factor authentication for contributors since March 2023 and it is enabled on the maintainer account; the second factor is GitHub Mobile push approval, a challenge-response to a registered device rather than SMS. It gates repository settings changes and access to private vulnerability reports alike.
osps_ac_02_01_justification: GitHub assigns the lowest available permissions to new collaborators by default and requires explicit assignment of anything more. The repository currently has no collaborators beyond the maintainer.
osps_ac_03_01_justification: A main-protection repository ruleset blocks direct pushes to main. Every change — including the maintainer's own — lands through a pull request with the full gate green as a required status check. A require-signed-commits ruleset applies in addition.
osps_ac_03_02_justification: The main-protection ruleset blocks deletion of the primary branch outright, which is stricter than requiring confirmation of intent.
osps_ac_04_01_justification: Every workflow declares permissions: contents: read at the top level, so a job that specifies nothing inherits read-only. Elevated scopes are granted per job and annotated inline with the reason — packages: write only on the jobs that push, id-token: write only where Sigstore needs it.
osps_ac_04_02_justification: Scopes are granted per job and each grant carries an inline comment saying why: packages: write only on the jobs that push an image, id-token: write only on the job that needs Sigstore OIDC. Everything else inherits the top-level contents: read. Runners additionally enforce egress-policy: block and disable-sudo where applicable.
osps_br_01_01_justification: Workflows do not interpolate untrusted event metadata into shell steps. This is enforced rather than asserted: zizmor runs at --persona=pedantic on every commit and in CI, and CodeQL analyses the workflows as its actions language, both of which flag template injection from untrusted contexts. actionlint runs alongside them.
osps_br_01_03_justification: Pull-request CI runs on the pull_request trigger rather than pull_request_target, so untrusted code never executes with access to the base repository's privileged context. Workflows default to contents: read with elevated scopes granted per job, every checkout sets persist-credentials: false, and the publish workflow — the only one holding packages: write and id-token: write — runs on push to main and on schedule, never on contributor code.
osps_br_01_04_justification: No collaborator-supplied value is interpolated into a shell step. Enforced rather than asserted: zizmor at --persona=pedantic and actionlint run on every commit and in CI, and CodeQL analyses the workflows as its actions language — the combination is specifically good at template injection, which is the form this failure takes in GitHub Actions.
osps_br_02_01_justification: Every published image carries a unique identifier by construction: its immutable OCI manifest digest, plus a :sha-<commit> tag giving per-commit traceability. A tag-immutability repository ruleset prevents any tag from moving, and consumers pin digests. The project deliberately has no semantic version surface — its version is the postgres major plus three extension pins — but uniqueness is absolute rather than merely conventional.
osps_br_02_02_justification: Every asset is identified by content: each layer and each per-architecture manifest carries its own sha256 digest, and the multi-arch index digest commits to all of them. The index is additionally tagged :sha-<commit>, associating the whole set with the exact commit that produced it. Nothing in a publish is identified by anything mutable.
osps_br_03_01_justification: Every official channel is HTTPS-only: the repository and issue tracker on GitHub, and the image at ghcr.io. No project channel is served over plain HTTP.
osps_br_03_02_justification: The image is distributed from GHCR over HTTPS and authenticated beyond transport: every digest is signed keylessly by the org signer with build provenance, and consumers pin digests. README 'Verifying a digest' gives the gh attestation verify command. https://github.com/monumental-archive/monumental-archive-db/blob/main/README.md#verifying-a-digest
osps_br_04_01_justification: The project creates no official releases. It is a rolling publisher: fixes land on main and a new digest publishes, with no version tags and no maintained back-branches, stated as a deliberate exclusion in https://github.com/CarlAllenn/monumental-archive-db/blob/main/docs/roadmap.md. What exists instead: every published digest is traceable to exactly one commit through its :sha-<commit> tag, the history is conventional-commit formatted so the functional and security changes between any two digests are readable with git log, and security modifications specifically are published as GitHub security advisories naming the fixing digest.
osps_br_05_01_justification: Dependencies are ingested entirely through standardized tooling: apt from PGDG and Debian for the extensions, the OCI registry protocol for both digest-pinned images, and mise for the development toolchain. Nothing is fetched with ad-hoc curl-to-shell, and there is no vendored or hand-copied dependency anywhere.
osps_br_06_01_justification: Each publish is an OCI index whose manifests list every layer by sha256; the index carries build provenance signed by the org signer (Sigstore keyless), each per-architecture digest carries its SBOM attestation, and a signed VEX decision names them. All are retrievable by digest. https://github.com/monumental-archive/monumental-archive-db/blob/main/README.md#verifying-a-digest
osps_br_07_01_justification: gitleaks runs on every commit through the lefthook hooks and over the full repository history in CI (task scan:secrets). Structurally there is also very little to leak: no long-lived registry or signing credential exists, because GHCR uses the workflow run's own token and signing is keyless.
osps_br_07_02_justification: docs/continuity.md is the secrets policy in operational form: an asset table naming every credential the project uses, where it is stored, who can reach it, and how it is rotated or recreated — including the one standing token, whose expiry is designed to fail loudly rather than silently under-claim. The policy is short because the architecture removes most secrets: publishing is keyless via OIDC and trusted publishing, and no signing key exists to store. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/continuity.md
osps_do_01_01_justification: The README documents everything needed to use the image: the reference to pull, the tag and digest policy, the baked server configuration (shared_preload_libraries and wal_level=logical), the non-root user, the emptied initdb directory, and the signature verification command. Runtime environment variables are the official postgres image's and are documented upstream. https://github.com/CarlAllenn/monumental-archive-db#readme
osps_do_02_01_justification: SUPPORT.md and the repository's issue forms document how to report a defect, and SECURITY.md documents the separate private path for vulnerabilities. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/SUPPORT.md
osps_do_03_01_justification: README 'Verifying a digest' gives the exact gh attestation verify command (owner, signer workflow, source ref) a consumer runs to check integrity and provenance; digests published before the 2026-08-21 transfer have their own recorded cosign command beside it. https://github.com/monumental-archive/monumental-archive-db/blob/main/README.md#verifying-a-digest
osps_do_03_02_justification: The verification command names the expected author precisely: --signer-workflow monumental-archive/signer/.github/workflows/sign.yml and --source-ref refs/heads/main, so an attestation minted by any other workflow or ref does not verify. https://github.com/monumental-archive/monumental-archive-db/blob/main/README.md#verifying-a-digest
osps_do_04_01_justification: The org SECURITY.md (served to this repository, which carries no copy) states support scope: only the latest receives fixes, by rolling forward. For this image that is the latest published digest: README 'Tags' explains there are no versions, and the image is republished on every merge and weekly. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/SECURITY.md#supported-versions-and-end-of-life
osps_do_05_01_justification: The same section states it without euphemism: only the latest published digest is supported. A superseded digest receives no further security updates — it is immutable and remains exactly as published. Because consumers pin digests, this is a property they control directly: a fix reaches you when you bump the digest.
osps_do_06_01_justification: Selection: postgres plus exactly three extensions, a fourth being a recorded governance decision (docs/roadmap.md). Obtaining: docs/decisions/0001-own-the-installation.md explains why PostGIS and pgaudit are installed from PGDG. Tracking: Renovate under the org preset, every FROM pinned by digest and enforced by lint:from-digests. https://github.com/monumental-archive/monumental-archive-db/blob/main/docs/decisions/0001-own-the-installation.md
osps_do_07_01_justification: README 'Development': mise trust && mise install && mise run hooks:install, then mise run ci for the gate; docker build plus bash scripts/db-image-smoke.sh builds and proves the image by hand. The only prerequisite mise does not install is a container engine. https://github.com/monumental-archive/monumental-archive-db/blob/main/README.md#development
osps_gv_01_01_justification: docs/continuity.md carries an asset table naming who holds each sensitive resource — organisation ownership, the tag-mint App key, registry accounts, the one standing token — and what happens to each if that person is unavailable. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/continuity.md
osps_gv_01_02_justification: GOVERNANCE.md carries a 'Roles and responsibilities' table naming three roles - maintainer/owner, contributor, automation - and the responsibilities of each, and it is served from the organisation's .github repository as a default community health file so it applies to every repository that does not carry its own. Who holds the maintainer role is explicit: the @monumental-archive/owners team, which CODEOWNERS routes every review to. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#roles-and-responsibilities
osps_gv_02_01_justification: The GitHub issue tracker is the public forum for proposed changes and usage obstacles, and pull requests carry design discussion. https://github.com/CarlAllenn/monumental-archive-db/issues
osps_gv_03_01_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md explains the contribution process: open an issue first for anything large, pull requests for small self-contained fixes, Conventional Commits, DCO sign-off, a green `mise run ci`, squash merge. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
osps_gv_03_02_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md includes a 'Requirements for acceptable contributions' section: pull request only, a green `mise run ci`, Conventional Commits with imperative lowercase subjects under 72 columns, DCO sign-off, squash merge. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
osps_gv_04_01_justification: GOVERNANCE.md section 'Escalation and permissions' carries the policy: a collaborator is reviewed before being granted any escalated permission. Concretely, before an account joins @monumental-archive/owners or receives write access anywhere, the maintainer reviews who they are, why the access is needed and what the smallest sufficient grant is - and the grant is then recorded in the settings-as-code baseline so drift is auditable. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#escalation-and-permissions
osps_le_01_01_justification: Every commit must carry a Developer Certificate of Origin 1.1 sign-off asserting legal authorisation. The commit-msg hook catches a missing trailer locally and lint:dco fails the gate, with no exemption list — automation signs off too.
osps_le_02_01_justification: AGPL-3.0-only, which is both OSI-approved and an FSF free software licence.
osps_le_02_02_justification: The released asset is the container image. Its constituent software is licensed under the PostgreSQL licence (PostgreSQL, pgaudit), GPL-2.0 (PostGIS), MIT OR Apache-2.0 (edtf_postgres) and the various Debian package licences — all free software licences meeting the OSI and FSF definitions.
osps_le_03_01_justification: https://github.com/CarlAllenn/monumental-archive-db/blob/main/LICENSE at the repository root. The repository is additionally REUSE 3.3 compliant, with full licence texts in https://github.com/CarlAllenn/monumental-archive-db/tree/main/LICENSES and SPDX headers throughout, verified by reuse lint as its own CI job.
osps_le_03_02_justification: Licences ship inside the released image itself, under the Debian convention at /usr/share/doc/*/copyright for every installed package. The image additionally carries an SPDX SBOM attestation generated at build time. Worth stating precisely: no AGPL-covered material from this repository ships inside the image — what this project contributes is the assembly recipe (the Dockerfile and two scripts), which stays in the source repository under https://github.com/CarlAllenn/monumental-archive-db/blob/main/LICENSE
osps_qa_01_01_justification: https://github.com/CarlAllenn/monumental-archive-db — publicly readable at a stable URL, no authentication required.
osps_qa_01_02_justification: Full git history is public, with author and timestamp on every commit, and commits are signed under a require-signed-commits ruleset. Every change arrives through a pull request, so the review record is public alongside the diff.
osps_qa_02_01_justification: Direct dependencies are declared machine-readably and completely: two digest-pinned FROM lines and exact apt versions in ARG *_VERSION declarations in https://github.com/CarlAllenn/monumental-archive-db/blob/main/Dockerfile, each with a # renovate: comment above it so the pin cannot silently lose automated coverage. Development toolchain dependencies are pinned in mise.toml with mise.lock.
osps_qa_02_02_justification: Every publish produces an SBOM per architecture from the pushed digest in the registry, refusing one with versionless PURLs, and attests it against that image digest; the index carries build provenance. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/dependency-track.md#sboms-are-class-shaped-derived-from-what-the-class-ships
osps_qa_03_01_justification: Direct pushes to main are blocked by the main-protection ruleset, so every commit arrives through a pull request, and the full gate runs as required status checks that must pass before merge. The same tasks run locally on every commit through the lefthook hooks, so the checks are not first encountered in CI.
osps_qa_04_01_justification: The project is a single repository. There is no second codebase to enumerate.
osps_qa_04_02_justification: The project is a single repository with no subprojects.
osps_qa_05_01_justification: No generated executable artifacts are committed. The repository contains a Dockerfile, two shell scripts, configuration and documentation; everything executable in the published image is built or installed at build time and never checked in. Scorecard's Binary-Artifacts check scores 10.
osps_qa_05_02_justification: No binary artifacts of any kind are in version control, reviewable or otherwise — confirmed continuously by Scorecard's Binary-Artifacts check at 10.
osps_qa_06_01_justification: Every pull request runs the org gate (mise run ci). The continuous publish builds each architecture on native amd64 and arm64 runners and boots it with scripts/db-image-smoke.sh, proving the extensions load via pg_get_loaded_modules(), before any push, then proves the published bytes again by digest. https://github.com/monumental-archive/monumental-archive-db/actions
osps_qa_06_02_justification: README 'Development' states that mise run ci is exactly what the shared gate runs on a pull request, and how to build and smoke the image by hand; the image smoke runs in the publish path on every merge and on the weekly schedule. https://github.com/monumental-archive/monumental-archive-db/blob/main/README.md#development
osps_qa_06_03_justification: The org CONTRIBUTING.md item 3 (served to this repository) requires a change that adds or changes behaviour to add the check that holds it, and a bug fix to add the case that reproduced it. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#requirements-for-acceptable-contributions
osps_qa_07_01_justification: With a single maintainer there is no non-author human approval available, so this is not enforced. It is the headcount wall this project records rather than works around: the same boundary as Gold's two_person_review and SLSA Source L4, tracked as an open issue rather than quietly claimed. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/slsa-reference.md
osps_sa_01_01_justification: https://github.com/CarlAllenn/monumental-archive-db/blob/main/docs/assurance-case.md documents the actors and actions: the five trust boundaries (publish, build-stage, apt, in-image privilege, registry identity), the four supply-chain substitution points an adversary could target, what crosses each boundary and by what mechanism, and what is explicitly out of scope. https://github.com/CarlAllenn/monumental-archive-db/blob/main/docs/decisions/0001-own-the-installation.md carries the load-bearing architectural decision behind the design.
osps_sa_02_01_justification: The released asset's external interfaces are the PostgreSQL wire protocol on 5432, the environment-variable contract inherited unchanged from the official postgres image, the PGDATA volume, and the three extensions the image adds. All are documented in https://github.com/CarlAllenn/monumental-archive-db#readme, together with the baked server configuration (shared_preload_libraries and wal_level=logical) that changes behaviour relative to a stock postgres image — which is the part a consumer could not infer from upstream documentation.
osps_sa_03_01_justification: Two documents, deliberately different in kind. https://github.com/CarlAllenn/monumental-archive-db/blob/main/docs/assurance-case.md is the standing assessment: threat model in order of exposure, the four substitution points, and a table of weakness classes with countermeasures and evidence. https://github.com/CarlAllenn/monumental-archive-db/blob/main/docs/security-review-2026.md is a dated assessment performed 2026-08-09 against a specific commit, with five findings and a disposition for each — including two that resulted in fixes.
osps_sa_03_02_justification: https://github.com/CarlAllenn/monumental-archive-db/blob/main/docs/assurance-case.md#threat-model is an explicit threat model ordered by exposure, naming supply-chain substitution as primary and enumerating its four distinct points (base image, extension build stage, apt layer, published manifest), then CI compromise, known-vulnerable OS packages, and configuration that misleads a consumer — each with what is explicitly out of scope. The attack surface analysis is the trust-boundary section, which states what crosses each boundary and by what mechanism. https://github.com/CarlAllenn/monumental-archive-db/blob/main/docs/security-review-2026.md then tests that model against the implementation on a dated pass and records where it did not hold.
osps_vm_01_01_justification: SECURITY.md is the coordinated disclosure policy and it states the timeframe: private reporting through the repository's Security tab, acknowledgement within 14 days, and what the reporter can expect afterwards. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/SECURITY.md
osps_vm_02_01_justification: SECURITY.md names the security contact and the reporting channel: private vulnerability reporting through the repository's Security tab, with a 14-day acknowledgement commitment. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/SECURITY.md
osps_vm_03_01_justification: GitHub private vulnerability reporting is enabled and linked directly: https://github.com/CarlAllenn/monumental-archive-db/security/advisories/new — the report stays private until a fix ships. An email fallback to the maintainer address on the commits is documented for anyone who cannot use it.
osps_vm_04_01_justification: Vulnerabilities in this image are published as GitHub Security Advisories on this repository, per the org SECURITY.md; none has been found. Dependency advisory decisions are published as signed OpenVEX attestations against each digest. https://github.com/monumental-archive/monumental-archive-db/security/advisories
osps_vm_04_02_justification: Every continuous publish derives a VEX document for the pushed digests with stele derive vex from the canon's decisions keyed by package@version, refuses to publish while any advisory in the SBOM is undecided, and attests the OpenVEX document against the digests. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/dependency-track.md#the-exit-vex-signed-never-an-override
osps_vm_05_01_justification: The threshold is zero undecided: docs/dependency-track.md requires every advisory in a published artifact's SBOM to carry a decision (fixed, or not_affected with a justification) before it publishes, and the continuous path enforces that on every publish. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/dependency-track.md#where-l2-is-met-by-construction-not-cadence
osps_vm_05_02_justification: The policy is enforced at the release boundary, not merely stated: the release path refuses to publish with an undecided advisory in its SBOM. It has already blocked a real release in the lab rather than being theoretical. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/dependency-track.md
osps_vm_05_03_justification: Automatically on every change: dependency-review on every pull request, and the org gate's lint:trivy (misconfiguration and secrets) and lint:from-digests; on every publish the image SBOM's advisories gate the push. Renovate raises updates. https://github.com/monumental-archive/monumental-archive-db/blob/main/.github/workflows/dependency-review.yml
osps_vm_06_01_justification: SECURITY.md section 'Static analysis policy' defines the remediation threshold, and it is zero: any SAST finding - CodeQL, the lint belt, zizmor and peers - fails the CI gate, and a red gate cannot merge, so findings are remediated or explicitly and reviewably suppressed with a written reason before the change lands. There is no severity triage queue for static findings because there is no state in which one is outstanding on a default branch. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/SECURITY.md
osps_vm_06_02_justification: All changes are evaluated automatically and blocked on violation by the org gate: hadolint at every severity on the Dockerfile, shellcheck and shfmt on the scripts, actionlint and zizmor on the workflows, trivy misconfiguration and gitleaks secret scans, plus CodeQL's actions analysis. Configs are delivered by the belt, so there is no local copy to weaken. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/SECURITY.md#static-analysis-policy
regression_tests_added50_justification: No defect in this repository's own software was fixed in the window. Measured 2026-11-16: nine fix-typed commits on main in the last six months. Seven fixed CI configuration (egress allowlists, a buildkit mirror, a lychee ignore, the level stub, a smoke-script startup race). Two fixed real supply-chain defects, the cosign identity anchor (#6) and the edtf attestation-gate ref anchor (#17, security review F-1), and neither added a test; both were in publish code the 2026-08-21 transfer deleted, so the code they fixed no longer exists here. Publishing now runs through the org's continuous workflow, whose tests live in the canon. The org CONTRIBUTING.md item 3 requires the reproducing case for future fixes.
release_notes_justification: There are no releases: this image is a continuous publisher with no version surface (README 'Tags'). Each digest is traceable to its commit through its build provenance. https://github.com/monumental-archive/monumental-archive-db/blob/main/README.md#tags
release_notes_vulns_justification: Follows from release_notes: there are no release notes. Vulnerability fixes are announced as GitHub security advisories with the fixing digest named in the advisory.
repo_distributed_justification: git, a distributed version control system, hosted on GitHub.
repo_interim_justification: Every change lands as an individual commit through a pull request; interim versions are available between releases by construction, since the project publishes continuously rather than in drops.
repo_track_justification: Full history is tracked in git.
report_archive_justification: https://github.com/CarlAllenn/monumental-archive-db/issues?q=is%3Aissue — the full issue archive is public, open and closed.
report_process_justification: Bugs and feature requests go to this repository's issue tracker through the org issue forms; the org SUPPORT.md says where to ask, and security problems go through private vulnerability reporting per the org SECURITY.md. https://github.com/monumental-archive/monumental-archive-db/issues/new/choose
report_responses_justification: Issues are triaged and answered by the maintainer; the public tracker is the response record.
require_2FA_justification: GitHub has required two-factor authentication for contributors since March 2023, and the maintainer account has it enabled. Changing the central repository requires it, as does access to private vulnerability reports.
roles_responsibilities_justification: GOVERNANCE.md carries a 'Roles and responsibilities' table naming three roles - maintainer/owner, contributor, automation - and what each is responsible for. Who holds the maintainer role is unambiguous: the @monumental-archive/owners team, which CODEOWNERS routes every review to in every repository, and joining that team is what becoming a maintainer concretely means. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#roles-and-responsibilities
secure_2FA_justification: The second factor is GitHub Mobile push approval — a challenge-response to a registered device over an encrypted channel, where the secret is device-bound rather than a shared seed. It is not SMS, and it is not weaker than TOTP.
security_review_justification: https://github.com/CarlAllenn/monumental-archive-db/blob/main/docs/security-review-2026.md — performed 2026-08-09 against commit 8f4b0fe. Scope: the Dockerfile, the upstream attestation gate, the smoke test, the publish workflow (ordering invariant, signing identity, token scopes), CI runner hardening and egress policy, the repository rulesets, and the remediation model. Method: manual reading of the whole security-relevant surface, plus direct verification of live claims rather than reading the prose describing them. Five findings, each with a disposition. F-1 (moderate): the upstream attestation gate constrained the signer workflow path but not the ref, the same weakness fixed on our own cosign identity in #6 — fixed in #17 by deriving the expected release tag from the pin being checked. F-2 (low): the documented seven-day exposure claim was broader than the mechanism delivers, since a digest-pinned base is not refreshed by a cache-free rebuild — scoped in #18. F-3: egress allowlists inherited rather than derived, already tracked as #12. F-4 and F-5 informational and accepted. The review also records what the pass tried to break and could not, and re-affirms the residual risks rather than closing them.
signed_releases_justification: Every published digest is signed keylessly by the org signer (Sigstore; no private key at rest anywhere) with build provenance, and carries a signed VEX decision. README 'Verifying a digest' documents verification with the signer workflow and source ref pinned. There are no versioned releases; the signed unit is the digest. https://github.com/monumental-archive/monumental-archive-db/blob/main/README.md#verifying-a-digest
sites_https_justification: The project site (GitHub) and the distribution point (GHCR) are HTTPS-only.
sites_password_security_justification: The project operates no site of its own that authenticates external users. The project site and repository are GitHub and the distribution point is GHCR; all authentication is handled by GitHub, and this project stores no user credentials anywhere.
small_tasks_justification: No open issue in this repository is labelled good first issue or help wanted today. https://github.com/monumental-archive/monumental-archive-db/issues
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: zizmor checks the workflows for common CI vulnerability classes (template injection, excessive permissions, untrusted checkout), CodeQL's actions analysis covers the same surface, trivy's misconfiguration rules cover the Dockerfile, and gitleaks covers committed secrets; all run on every pull request.
static_analysis_fixed_justification: No outstanding findings. The gate fails on any finding and there is no bypass path.
static_analysis_justification: hadolint on the Dockerfile, shellcheck and shfmt on the scripts, actionlint and zizmor on the workflows, trivy misconfiguration and gitleaks secret scans, all in the org gate on every pull request; CodeQL additionally analyses the workflows in its actions language. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/SECURITY.md#static-analysis-policy
static_analysis_often_justification: On every commit through the lefthook hooks, and again on every pull request in CI.
test_branch_coverage80_justification: Same as test_statement_coverage90: no application code and no FLOSS tool that can measure branch coverage of an image assembly.
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: GitHub Actions runs the full gate on every push and pull request, and the publish workflow additionally builds and smokes per-architecture on native amd64 and arm64 runners before any push, then re-proves the published bytes pulled back by digest. https://github.com/CarlAllenn/monumental-archive-db/actions
test_invocation_justification: bash scripts/db-image-smoke.sh <image> runs the test suite against a built image, and mise run ci runs the whole gate; both are in README 'Development'. https://github.com/monumental-archive/monumental-archive-db/blob/main/README.md#development
test_justification: https://github.com/CarlAllenn/monumental-archive-db/blob/main/scripts/db-image-smoke.sh — boots the built image and proves the extensions actually load, asserting against pg_get_loaded_modules() rather than \dx, because \dx reports what is installable rather than what is loaded.
test_most_justification: There is no application code — the deliverable is a Dockerfile and the image it produces — and the smoke test asserts every claim the image makes about its own contents. Policy is that a change to what the image contains must come with an assertion that fails without it.
test_policy_justification: The org CONTRIBUTING.md item 3 (served here) requires a change that adds or changes behaviour to add the check that holds it; for this image that is a smoke assertion in scripts/db-image-smoke.sh that fails without the change. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#requirements-for-acceptable-contributions
test_policy_mandated_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md, 'Requirements for acceptable contributions' item 3, is the formal written policy: a change that adds or changes behaviour adds the check that holds it - a test that fails without the change where a test suite exists, and a lint, audit task or workflow assertion in configuration and policy repositories. It is stated as policy: the gate's checks are the specification, and functionality nothing enforces is functionality the next change may silently remove. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
test_statement_coverage80_justification: This criterion is conditioned on at least one FLOSS tool being able to measure it, and for a Dockerfile there is none — there is no application code here to instrument. What is testable is the published artifact's behaviour, which the smoke test asserts directly against a running server.
test_statement_coverage90_justification: Conditioned on at least one FLOSS tool being able to measure it; for a Dockerfile there is none. There is no application code in this repository to instrument — the only executable content authored here is two shell scripts, and what is testable is the assembled artifact's runtime behaviour, which the smoke test asserts directly against a live server.
tests_are_added_justification: Required by the policy above and checked at review; adding an extension without its assertion is called out as the failure mode that lets a later refactor silently drop it.
tests_documented_added_justification: Stated in CONTRIBUTING as a requirement for an acceptable contribution, not as a suggestion.
two_person_review_justification: With a single maintainer, no proposed modification is reviewed by a person other than its author. This is the Source L4 and Gold boundary for this project and is recorded as headcount-blocked in docs/slsa-reference.md; it is watched as an issue rather than papered over. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/slsa-reference.md
updateable_reused_components_justificati: Nothing is vendored, forked or copied in. Every reused component is an external pin that Renovate can bump in place — the two images by digest and the apt packages by exact version — so updating a vulnerable component is a one-line change with no patch to rebase.
version_semver_justification: Deliberate. This image has no version surface of its own — its version is the postgres major plus three extension pins, and its changes are pin bumps. Stated as a standing exclusion in https://github.com/CarlAllenn/monumental-archive-db/blob/main/docs/roadmap.md
version_tags_justification: Same reason as version_semver: no version tags by design. Per-commit :sha-<commit> tags and immutable digests provide the traceability that version tags would.
version_tags_signed_justification: There are no version tags to sign; none exist by design (README 'Tags'). The signed unit is the digest: commits are signed and enforced by ruleset, tags are immutable by ruleset, and each digest is signed by the org signer. https://github.com/monumental-archive/monumental-archive-db/blob/main/README.md#tags
version_unique_justification: Every published image is uniquely identified by its immutable manifest digest, and additionally carries a :sha-<commit> tag for traceability. Consumers pin digests, and a tag-immutability repository ruleset prevents any tag from moving.
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed_justifica: No known unfixed critical vulnerability is shipped: every publish, including the weekly rebuild, gates on each advisory in the image SBOM having a decision, and a fixable one is fixed by the rebuild or a pin bump. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/docs/dependency-track.md#where-l2-is-met-by-construction-not-cadence
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: The commitment is seven days rather than sixty. PostGIS's transitive OS dependencies cannot be pinned by anyone, so remediation is a weekly cache-free rebuild that re-resolves that layer from trixie-security with every deliberate pin intact. Reasoning: https://github.com/CarlAllenn/monumental-archive-db/blob/main/docs/decisions/0001-own-the-installation.md
vulnerability_report_credit_justificatio: No vulnerability report has been resolved in the last 12 months, so there is no reporter to credit. The org SECURITY.md commits to crediting reporters.
vulnerability_report_private_justificati: GitHub private vulnerability reporting is enabled: https://github.com/CarlAllenn/monumental-archive-db/security/advisories/new — the report stays private until a fix ships.
vulnerability_report_process_justificati: SECURITY.md publishes the process: private reporting through the repository's Security tab. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/SECURITY.md
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: No vulnerability report has been received in the last 6 months (this repository has no security advisories). The org SECURITY.md commits to acknowledgement within 14 days.
vulnerability_response_process_justifica: SECURITY.md documents the process end to end: private reporting through the repository's Security tab, acknowledgement within 14 days, what to expect afterwards, and the scope. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/SECURITY.md
warnings_fixed_justification: The gate fails on any warning and there are no bypass flags — fixing tool output is explicitly never optional. Enforced twice: locally by lefthook git hooks on every commit, remotely by required status checks on main.
warnings_justification: The belt runs every linter at its strictest: hadolint fails at every severity including style, shellcheck and shfmt on the scripts, actionlint and zizmor on the workflows; any finding reds the gate. https://github.com/monumental-archive/.github/blob/main/SECURITY.md#static-analysis-policy
warnings_strict_justification: Every linter runs at its strictest configured setting, zizmor at --persona=pedantic in particular, and the gate fails on any output with no bypass available.
